title: Transient ischaemic attack: immediate management and the carotid pathway

header.contentArea: Vascular surgery: carotid disease and TIA (examiner viva with a duplex report)
guidelineVersions: NICE NG128 Stroke and TIA in over 16s (May 2019, updated April 2022)
DVLA Assessing fitness to drive: neurological disorders (updated November 2025)

related.why: Carotid sheath and cranial nerve anatomy for carotid endarterectomy
Intermittent claudication: the same atherosclerotic risk factors

brief.role: Core surgical trainee on call for vascular surgery
brief.scenario: Mr Ryan Colquhoun, 72, had 20 minutes of weakness of his right arm and slurred speech at 08:00 today. It has fully resolved and examination now is normal. He has hypertension and smokes 20 cigarettes a day.
brief.task: Discuss his diagnosis and management with the examiner, who will give you further results.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Resolved focal deficit: suspected TIA. Aspirin now, specialist within 24 hours, image the carotid, fix the risk factors.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calculating ABCD2 to decide urgency, or a CT head for everyone.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Suspected left carotid territory TIA. I'd check his glucose and give aspirin 300 mg now."

grid.label: Diagnosis and territory
grid.fail: Calls it a stroke, or reassures because symptoms have gone.
grid.pass: Suspected TIA in the left carotid territory: right arm weakness with speech disturbance, fully resolved.
grid.high: Excludes mimics: glucose, seizure, migraine aura; knows MRI can still show infarction after full recovery.

grid.label: Immediate antiplatelet
grid.fail: Leaves antiplatelet treatment for the clinic.
grid.pass: Aspirin 300 mg daily, started immediately, unless contraindicated.
grid.high: Asks about anticoagulants, bleeding and aspirin allergy before giving it, and gives it in the department.

grid.label: Referral urgency
grid.fail: Uses the ABCD2 score to decide how soon he is seen.
grid.pass: Refers immediately to be seen by a stroke specialist within 24 hours of symptom onset.
grid.high: States NICE advises against scores such as ABCD2 because they do not reliably separate low from high risk.

grid.label: Brain and carotid imaging
grid.fail: Requests a CT head for every suspected TIA.
grid.pass: No CT unless an alternative diagnosis CT could detect is suspected; MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging considered on the day of specialist assessment.
grid.high: Prioritises urgent carotid imaging for any candidate for surgery, plus ECG for atrial fibrillation.

grid.label: Interpret the duplex and decide on surgery
grid.fail: Ignores which side is symptomatic, or operates on any stenosis.
grid.pass: Left ICA stenosis 50 to 99% (NASCET) on the symptomatic side: urgent referral for carotid endarterectomy plus best medical treatment.
grid.high: Checks the report states NASCET or ECST; below 50% NASCET, best medical treatment only; the asymptomatic right side is not the target.

grid.label: Best medical treatment
grid.pass: Antiplatelet therapy, high-intensity statin, blood pressure control, smoking cessation, and checks for diabetes and atrial fibrillation.
grid.high: Offers smoking cessation support today and explains that surgery adds to, not replaces, medical treatment.

grid.label: Driving and safety-netting
grid.fail: Gives no advice on driving or recurrence.
grid.pass: No driving for 1 month as a car driver; call 999 immediately if symptoms return.
grid.high: A single TIA does not need DVLA notification for a car licence; bus or lorry licences have stricter rules.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No driving for a month, and call 999 if symptoms come back.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A suspected left hemisphere TIA. I'd check his glucose and ask about headache or seizure to exclude a mimic. Even with full recovery, MRI can show a small infarct.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Yes, 300 mg here in the department, once I've checked he isn't on an anticoagulant and has no bleeding or aspirin allergy.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NICE advises against using it: scores don't reliably separate low from high risk, so everyone is seen within 24 hours.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Which imaging matters most for you?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Urgent carotid duplex, because it decides whether he needs surgery. An ECG too, as atrial fibrillation would change treatment to anticoagulation.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Duplex: 75% stenosis of the left ICA; 30% on the right.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd check the report states NASCET. The left is the symptomatic side and meets the threshold; the right doesn't. Below 50% NASCET he'd have medical treatment only.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: He asks if the operation fixes everything.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Surgery adds to tablets, it doesn't replace them. Stopping smoking is the biggest thing he can do, and I'd refer him for support today.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: For his car licence, no driving for a month and no need to tell the DVLA. Bus licences have stricter rules, so he must not drive the bus and must check them.

failures.move: Waiting for clinic before starting aspirin.
failures.consequence: Stroke risk is highest in the first days, when aspirin gives most benefit.

failures.move: Using a low ABCD2 score to delay assessment.
failures.consequence: A high-risk patient waits and may have a disabling stroke.

failures.move: Offering surgery on the asymptomatic side.
failures.consequence: Exposes him to operative risk without treating the source of his TIA.

failures.move: Discussing surgery without statin, blood pressure and smoking treatment.
failures.consequence: Recurrent vascular events are more likely.

recovery.line: Actually NICE advises against using ABCD2 for urgency; he should be seen within 24 hours regardless.

recovery.when: You asked for a CT head
recovery.line: A CT only helps if I suspect an alternative diagnosis; carotid imaging is what changes his management.

knowledge.fact: Suspected TIA: aspirin 300 mg immediately unless contraindicated; specialist within 24 hours.
Do not use ABCD2 or other scores to decide urgency.
No CT unless an alternative diagnosis CT could detect is suspected; consider same-day MRI after specialist assessment.
Symptomatic 50 to 99% NASCET: urgent referral for endarterectomy plus best medical treatment; below 50%: no surgery. Reports must state NASCET or ECST.
Car drivers must not drive for 1 month after a single TIA; DVLA need not be told.

recall.think: Early stroke from a symptomatic carotid stenosis.
recall.say: "Suspected left carotid territory TIA: aspirin now, specialist within 24 hours."
recall.finish: Urgent endarterectomy plus best medical treatment.

sources.name: NICE NG128: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management
sources.supports: Aspirin 300 mg started immediately for suspected TIA unless contraindicated (1.1.4); refer immediately to be seen within 24 hours of symptom onset (1.1.5); do not use scoring systems such as ABCD2 to assess risk or urgency (1.1.6); no CT brain unless an alternative diagnosis CT could detect is suspected (1.1.8); consider same-day MRI with diffusion-weighted and blood-sensitive sequences after specialist assessment (1.1.9); urgent carotid imaging for candidates for endarterectomy; symptomatic stenosis 50-99% NASCET: assess and refer urgently for carotid endarterectomy plus best medical treatment (1.2.4); under 50% NASCET: no surgery, best medical treatment (1.2.5); reports must state NASCET or ECST criteria

sources.name: DVLA. Assessing fitness to drive: a guide for medical professionals. Neurological disorders
sources.supports: Single TIA, Group 1 (car and motorcycle): must not drive for 1 month; need not notify DVLA

partner.opening: Mr Colquhoun had 20 minutes of right arm weakness and slurred speech this morning. He is now back to normal. What is the diagnosis, and what would you do?
partner.actorBrief: You are the examiner. Give results only when asked. If the candidate mentions ABCD2 or a CT head, ask why.

reveals.trigger: Asks for glucose, ECG or observations
reveals.finding: Capillary glucose 6.1 mmol/L. ECG sinus rhythm 78. BP 164/92. Neurological examination normal.
Ramipril only. No anticoagulant, no bleeding history, no allergies.
Carotid duplex: left ICA stenosis 75% (NASCET criteria), heterogeneous plaque; right ICA 30%.

push.question: What is the diagnosis?
push.expect: Suspected TIA, left carotid territory; exclude mimics such as hypoglycaemia.

push.question: How urgently must he be seen, and would ABCD2 help?
push.expect: Within 24 hours; do not use ABCD2 to decide.

push.question: Does he need a CT head?
push.expect: Not unless an alternative diagnosis is suspected; MRI after specialist assessment; urgent carotid imaging.

push.question: Interpret the duplex. What next?
push.expect: Symptomatic 50-99% NASCET: urgent endarterectomy referral plus best medical treatment.

push.question: What advice before he goes?
push.expect: No driving for 1 month; 999 if symptoms recur.

curveballs.safeAnswer: A cardioembolic source is possible: discuss anticoagulation with the stroke team; carotid imaging is still needed.

curveballs.prompt: The duplex shows the left ICA is occluded.
curveballs.safeAnswer: An occluded artery is not treated by endarterectomy: best medical treatment and stroke team follow-up.

curveballs.prompt: He has another episode of arm weakness while waiting.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Treat as a possible acute stroke: call the stroke team immediately for urgent brain imaging and thrombolysis assessment.
